transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess... I've just been taking on a lot lately. I volunteered for the historical society project, and... I don't know, I just kind of acted like I could run the whole fundraiser by myself. I started making all these quilt designs, calling up volunteers, making schedules... and I ended up promising deadlines that I, um, I just couldn't possibly meet. So, that's why I'm here.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling unusually energetic, upbeat, or like you needed much less sleep than usual, even while taking on all these tasks?

I suppose... yes. At first, I felt, um... almost glowing, I guess. Like every idea I had was just wonderful. But... well, if anyone questioned me about how I was doing it, I got a bit snappish. I just... I felt like they were standing in my way.
Have you ever had episodes like this before, or times in the past when you felt unusually depressed, low, or hopeless for an extended period?

I haven't really had... the energetic times before. But... yes, I've felt low. Since the quilt orders fell behind and, um, some conflicts blew up with the other volunteers... I've just been stuck in this very low, guilty place. It's been about nine months now, I think.
That period when you felt unusually energetic, upbeat, and full of ideas—about how many days in a row did that last?
I guess... it was a while. That whole overdriven stretch with the project... it went on for about five months, I think. Before everything just... fell apart.

During those five months when you felt unusually energetic and full of ideas, did it cause serious problems in your daily life or relationships—or did you ever need to be hospitalized or experience things like hearing or seeing things others didn't?

Well... I wasn't hospitalized or anything like that. And I didn't see things. But... yes, it caused problems. My husband... he's had to take over a lot of things. The household stuff, mostly. And... he's the one who has to deal with the historical society now. I just... I stopped keeping up with my commitments there. I couldn't face all those people who were waiting on me. So... he handles it.
During these past nine months of feeling low and guilty, have you had any thoughts of death or of harming yourself?

I... I wouldn't actually do anything to hurt myself. I don't have any sort of plan for that. But... sometimes I just think... it might be easier if I didn't wake up. Then my husband wouldn't have to keep cleaning up the messes I've made.

latest_inference.note: The manic-like episode caused clear functional impairment (husband had to take over household and organizational duties), consistent with a full manic (not hypomanic) episode, followed by a major depressive episode with passive suicidal ideation but no plan or psychotic features. This confirms Bipolar I Disorder, current episode depressed, moderate to severe without psychotic features.
